title: America’s Looming Debt Reckoning
gist: Kenneth Rogoff warns that with a federal deficit around 6% of GDP despite solid growth and little political appetite for consolidation, the US risks having few fiscal options when the next war, recession or financial crisis arrives, as high debt becomes dangerous once rising rates push up borrowing costs.

insights.claim: High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Interest-rate trajectory, not debt level alone, is the trigger to watch for US fiscal stress and term-premium risk.
insights.quote: High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond.

insights.claim: Despite solid growth, the US federal deficit is about 6% of GDP.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Running large pro-cyclical deficits in an expansion implies heavy Treasury supply and limited countercyclical room later.
insights.quote: Despite solid growth, the federal deficit is about 6% of GDP.

insights.claim: There is little political appetite to rein in the US deficit, and slowing down does not appear to be in President Donald Trump's playbook.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Absent fiscal consolidation, bond-market discipline may become the eventual constraint.
insights.quote: the option of slowing down does not appear to be in President Donald Trump’s playbook

themes.theme: Loss of fiscal space for the next crisis

insights.claim: The US risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession or financial crisis arrives because of its ballooning debt.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Reduced fiscal firepower could deepen future downturns and shift more burden onto monetary policy.
insights.quote: the United States risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession, or financial crisis arrives

insights.claim: America's fiscal position resembles a train hurtling along a twisting mountain track that no one will slow for fear of losing their job; even if it does not crash, there is little reason to keep pushing it.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Political incentives favor continued deficits, making a disorderly adjustment more likely than a planned one.
insights.quote: America’s fiscal position is increasingly looking like a train hurtling along a twisting mountain track.
